Ruddy

RUD-ee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ruddy is having a healthy reddish color, especially in the face.

The sculptor spent hours mixing paint to capture the innkeeper's ruddy, weathered complexion.

Worked Example

After an hour of shoveling snow, his ruddy cheeks and nose made him look like he'd stepped out of a holiday card.

Ruddy specifically describes a healthy reddish tone in the skin, most often caused by cold, wind, or exertion.

How Ruddy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rosy

rosy: pink or reddish in a healthy-looking way

flushed

flushed: reddened in the face, often from heat, exertion, or emotion

Antonyms

pale

pale: having little color in the face; light-toned

pallid

pallid: unhealthily pale

How Strong Is It? — pinkish → flaming red → ruddy

pinkish vs. ruddy

pinkish vs. ruddy: Pinkish means having only a faint tinge of pink, a milder color than ruddy.

flaming red vs. ruddy

flaming red vs. ruddy: Flaming red describes an intensely bright red, well beyond the healthy glow of ruddy.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rud-

root — rud-: red (Old English rudu, related to read, 'red')

suffix — -dy

suffix — -dy: the -y ending: full of (the d doubles) (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Ruddy comes from Old English rudu, 'redness,' related to the word red, plus the -y ending meaning 'full of,' with the d doubled -- so a ruddy face is literally 'full of red,' glowing with healthy color.
